key_insight: The best-scoring agent checkpoint can forget how to solve tasks that earlier checkpoints handled successfully. Agentic-OPD uses these discarded checkpoints as teachers to recover overlooked capabilities through on-policy distillation.
problem_solved: Keeping only the best-validation checkpoint loses useful agent skills: across a GRPO training run, different checkpoints solve different problems, and their combined coverage exceeds that of any single checkpoint.
method: Compare problems solved by checkpoints from the same GRPO training run to identify forgotten capabilities.
Reuse earlier checkpoints as a teacher pool rather than discarding them.
Apply on-policy distillation to transfer teacher capabilities into the agent; implementation details are not available in the provided abstract excerpt.
impact: Checkpoint selection can hide valuable capabilities behind a single validation score. Reusing training checkpoints offers practitioners a route to broader task coverage without training a separate teacher pool.
visual_elements: Training timeline showing tasks gained and later forgotten across checkpoints.
Overlapping circles comparing the best checkpoint’s solved tasks with the union across checkpoints.
Teacher-pool diagram showing earlier checkpoints feeding knowledge into one student agent.
Task-by-checkpoint heatmap highlighting complementary successes and forgetting.
paper_title: Agentic-OPD: Recovering Forgotten Agent Capabilities via On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Tasks
paper_authors: Tingcheng Bian, Kangye Gong, Jinchang Luo, MingQuan Cheng, Feiran Liu
